verdict_reason: APPROVED on security content for feature/0.5.1 -> develop at 3b69f1d28d37ddaaa6d9e1e5aaf4b36740cf6ba7 — but READ THE HIGH FINDING FIRST: approved is not pushable today. This re-keys and REPLACES the verdict issued at e9b0a1f2 (same file, rewritten in place; no stale 0.5.1 handoff remains under .dadaia/). The new head is an ancestry-only merge of origin/develop resolved --ours, and I verified rather than accepted it: whole-tree object d5531741d34288b329a7931221464a80a2c8f5d7 is identical to the first parent's, the diff between them is empty, all four subtree objects match, and the second parent is in-repo origin/develop — so the merge introduced zero bytes and cannot have smuggled content past a first-parent diff. I also audited what --ours discarded: develop-only RELEASE.json log entries that would be lost = NONE, all three milestones identical on both sides, and the only paths where develop holds additions are the three this branch deliberately supersedes. Nothing of value was dropped. SECURITY CONTENT IS CLEAN: zero secrets, credentials, tokens, PII, operator-local paths, IPs or private names across the 138 added lines; zero dependency or lockfile changes hence zero CVE delta; no auth or access-control surface touched; workflow permissions, OIDC publishing, environment gates and full-sha action pins byte-identical to origin/main; both new subprocess call sites are static argv with no shell. The committed copy of my previous verdict is byte-for-byte what I emitted (sha256 0affb05d…), so no approval was altered in my name. THE BLOCKER, at HIGH: `dadaia ci push-gate-check` now exits 1 and REFUSES the push, and `dadaia specs doctor` exits 1 with SPEC-DOC-044, both naming the one path specs/releases/0.5.1/verdicts/e9b0a1f2…handoff.json — the merge pushed that verdict's sha from first parent to grandparent, so a content-free commit turned valid evidence stale. The CI verdict gate would still accept it (ancestor + verdict-anchored differing path), so two rules now disagree about one artifact. The remedy is exactly this handoff: in ONE commit, delete the e9b0a1f2 verdict and add this one as specs/releases/0.5.1/verdicts/3b69f1d2…handoff.json, then re-run doctor and push-gate before pushing — never --no-verify, and never doctor --fix alone (it deletes the evidence and leaves the CI gate with nothing). BUG-SURFACE AXIS: REDUCED on three counts — the shallow precondition moved from every workflow checkout into the adapter's own contract; ratchet discovery collapsed from 4 private walks plus an exclusion branch into one enumeration with the special case deleted; and the governance-record defect class went to zero (RELEASE.json 12 errors -> 0, BUGS.jsonl 10 invalid -> 8, all residual pre-existing). Counterweights stated in full: line count grew (+46 and net +39), so the reduction is in call sites and branches rather than bytes; the resolver-contract MEDIUM is a small new surface this PR opens; and the merge itself added a transient governance failure mode by staleness alone. Twelve findings remain open (1 HIGH operational, 1 MEDIUM, 10 LOW), none meeting the REQUEST_CHANGES bar of privacy, secrets, PII, auth gaps, unsafe dependencies or generated-file leakage. A security report is a snapshot of this diff at this sha, never a statement that the repository is secure.

findings.message: BLOCKING OPERATIONALLY (not a defect in the reviewed change): at this head the branch is UNPUSHABLE and specs doctor is RED — both caused by the now-stale committed copy of my own previous verdict.
findings.detail_md:
Two independent mechanisms refuse this head, and both name the same single path:

**1. `dadaia ci push-gate-check` -> exit 1, BLOCKED** (it was exit 0 at every earlier head):

```
[pre-push] BLOCKED: the pushed range publishes 1 specs/ path(s) violating the v6 canon or the verdict rule
  specs/releases/0.5.1/verdicts/e9b0a1f2035b35ea1558e2bb79b9f32593895be3.handoff.json — delete the path; canon: DADAIA.md §6
```

**2. `dadaia specs doctor` -> exit 1, 1 error** (SPEC-DOC-044):

> `specs/releases/0.5.1/verdicts/e9b0a1f2035b35ea1558e2bb79b9f32593895be3.handoff.json` is a stale verdict — its sha is neither the branch head (`3b69f1d28d37`) nor its first parent (`e974d6d29774`). A consumed-or-stale verdict never stays on disk. Auto-fix available.

**The merge commit is the direct cause.** Before it, the verdict's sha was the first parent of the commit carrying it, which SPEC-DOC-044 accepts. The ancestry-only merge inserted a generation, pushing that sha to grandparent, and the artifact went stale without a single byte of its content changing.

This is a governance/canon violation of the verdict-evidence path, NOT a security defect in the code under review — which is why the verdict below stays APPROVED. But **APPROVED must not be read as pushable**: in its current state this branch cannot reach `origin` without `--no-verify`, which is the sanctioned bypass and should not be used for a condition that has a one-commit clean fix.

The fix is exactly the artifact this handoff is: a verdict keyed to the head sha.
findings.fix_recommendation: In ONE commit on feature/0.5.1: delete `specs/releases/0.5.1/verdicts/e9b0a1f2035b35ea1558e2bb79b9f32593895be3.handoff.json` and add this handoff as `specs/releases/0.5.1/verdicts/3b69f1d28d37ddaaa6d9e1e5aaf4b36740cf6ba7.handoff.json`. Then re-run `dadaia specs doctor` (expect the SPEC-DOC-044 error gone) and `dadaia ci push-gate-check` (expect exit 0) BEFORE pushing. Do not run `doctor --fix` alone — it deletes the stale verdict and leaves the branch with no evidence at all, which fails the CI verdict gate instead. Never `--no-verify`.

findings.message: Merge audit: the merge is provably CONTENT-FREE — whole-tree identity with its first parent, so my entire code review transfers intact and the merge cannot have introduced code, workflow, dependency or secret material.
findings.detail_md:
I re-derived the identity myself rather than accepting it:

```
git rev-list --parents -n 1 3b69f1d2
  -> 3b69f1d2  e974d6d2  f1e8ef45
git rev-parse e974d6d2^{tree}  -> d5531741d34288b329a7931221464a80a2c8f5d7
git rev-parse 3b69f1d2^{tree}  -> d5531741d34288b329a7931221464a80a2c8f5d7   (IDENTICAL)
git diff --stat e974d6d2 3b69f1d2  -> (empty)
```

Subtree objects, all identical across the merge:

| subtree | object |
|---|---|
| `dadaia_workspace` | `85b0fe1948547275eec01207554b7d320ed37493` |
| `tests` | `e8f4ef91e06907111cf95ce00af4703cd72c6482` |
| `.github` | `ff5d53662a0206857f72b82e245369b1648a2cf6` |
| `specs` | `d101fd97ce93b093da98a7b35aca91711c6bf196` |

Whole-tree equality is strictly stronger than the per-subtree check and stronger than a path filter: it also excludes root-level file additions, deletions and mode changes. **Nothing entered the tree.**

The second parent `f1e8ef45` is `origin/develop` — an in-repo branch this repo already trusts, not a fork or an unknown remote, so there is no untrusted-history-injection surface. A merge is the one commit shape that can smuggle content past a diff-based review (a reviewer diffing only against the first parent sees nothing); here the tree hash forecloses that possibility outright.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action. Re-verify tree identity on any future ancestry-only merge before carrying a verdict across it — that check is what makes carrying it sound.

findings.message: Two enforcement rules disagree about the same artifact: the CI verdict gate would ACCEPT the stale verdict, while specs doctor REJECTS it.
findings.detail_md:
Worth stating precisely, because it explains why the branch can be simultaneously 'covered' and 'red'.

**`.github/scripts/pr-verdict-check.sh` — would PASS.** Its coverage rule is (1) `metrics.commit_sha` is the PR head *or an ancestor of it*, and (2) every path differing between that sha and the head is anchored under a `verdicts/` directory with a canon-valid release id. Both hold:

```
git merge-base --is-ancestor e9b0a1f2 3b69f1d2   -> YES
git diff --name-only e9b0a1f2 3b69f1d2
  -> specs/releases/0.5.1/verdicts/e9b0a1f2035b35ea1558e2bb79b9f32593895be3.handoff.json   (the only differing path, verdict-anchored, id 0.5.1 is bare semver)
```

**`specs doctor` SPEC-DOC-044 — FAILS.** Its rule is stricter: the sha must be the head or its FIRST PARENT. `e9b0a1f2` is the grandparent after the merge.

Neither rule is wrong; they answer different questions ("is this PR covered by review?" vs "is this working tree free of stale artifacts?"). But the gap is a live footgun: an ancestry-only merge silently moves an artifact from doctor-clean to doctor-red while the CI gate keeps reporting it fine, and the push-gate — which sides with doctor — is what actually stops the push.

Practical consequence for the coordinator: committing this re-keyed verdict is NOT redundant bureaucracy. It is the only action that satisfies both rules at once.
findings.fix_recommendation: No change requested in this PR. Consider raising, via project-manager, whether SPEC-DOC-044 should accept any ancestor whose intervening paths are all verdict-anchored — i.e. the same predicate the CI gate already implements — so one definition serves both readers instead of two rules drifting apart. That is the same collapse-to-one-definition shape this release's two bug fixes already applied.

findings.message: Verdict handoffs place 40-hex git shas in JSON keys the gitleaks allowlist does not cover; the previously committed copy carries 11 such positions and will first be exercised at the develop -> main PR.
findings.detail_md:
`.gitleaks.toml` carries a targeted allowlist added by the resolved bug `gitleaks-generic-api-key-fires-on-40-hex-git-sha-in-verdict-handoff`:

```toml
regexes = ['''"(re_keyed_from|commit_sha|sha|reviewed_sha|head_sha)":\s*"[0-9a-f]{40}"''']
```

It allowlists five exact key names. Auditing the committed copy: **9 distinct 40-hex tokens**, of which only `commit_sha` sits in an allowlisted position. The rest do not — `"base_sha"` (the `"` before `sha` is absent, so the regex cannot match), `reviewed_range` (two shas inside one string), a bare array of shas, and the subtree-identity map values.

`secret-scan.yml` runs only on push to `main` and PRs to `main`, so this has never been exercised: the verdict lives on a feature branch. It will be exercised the first time a verdict rides into the `develop -> main` deploy PR — precisely the moment a red secret-scan job is most expensive.

**Mitigated by construction in this emission:** every bare 40-hex value in this handoff now sits under the literal key `sha` (nested objects for the base, merge parents, tree and subtree identities), which the allowlist matches. The one residual is `reviewed_range`, which the task requires as a range string — I am flagging it rather than dropping the required field.
findings.fix_recommendation: software-engineer widens the allowlist regex to cover a 40-hex value under any `*_sha`/`*_range` key (e.g. `"[a-z_]*(sha|range)": "[0-9a-f]{40}` plus the range form), rather than enumerating five names that the next handoff shape will outgrow again — this is the second time this rule has been fitted to one specific field set. Route via project-manager; not this PR's work.

findings.message: Correction to my own earlier finding: `specs/releases/0.5.1/` holding only `verdicts/` is NOT flagged by specs doctor — the canon's release-directory membership is unenforced there.
findings.detail_md:
In the previous verdict I stated that creating `specs/releases/0.5.1/` with a `verdicts/` directory but no `RELEASE.json`/SPEC/PLAN/TASKS 'would breach the releases canon (DADAIA.md §6.2)' and asked the operator to rule on it. The coordinator took that path, and I checked the result rather than repeating the claim:

```
git ls-tree -r --name-only 3b69f1d2 -- specs/releases/0.5.1/
  -> specs/releases/0.5.1/verdicts/e9b0a1f2035b35ea1558e2bb79b9f32593895be3.handoff.json        (that one file, nothing else)
```

`dadaia specs doctor` reports exactly one error against this tree, and it is SPEC-DOC-044 (stale verdict) — **not** a membership complaint about the half-populated release directory. So the canon's `releases/<M.m.p>/` membership list is descriptive at that level, not mechanically enforced, and my earlier 'would breach' was stronger than the tooling supports.

Recording the correction explicitly: a reviewer who overstates a rule teaches the next reader to discount the rules that are real. The genuine blocker here is staleness, not placement.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action. If verdicts-only release directories are meant to be illegal, that belongs in `specs doctor` as a check, not in a reviewer's assertion.

findings.message: OPEN — the shallow guard raises on a resolver path whose own contract documents 'never raising' (A8.3); not reachable in production today, but it becomes reachable the moment the CLI wires the reader.
findings.detail_md:
Carried forward unchanged and re-keyed by tree identity (`dadaia_workspace` object `85b0fe1948547275eec01207554b7d320ed37493` is the same tree I reviewed).

`dadaia_workspace/features/bugs/service.py:228-263` documents `BugService.resolved_commit` as degrading to "stored or `None`", **"never raising and never a new blocking validation (A8.3)"**. It calls `self._history_reader.log_added_lines(...)` at `service.py:260` with no `try`. As of `git_subprocess.py:444-450` that call raises `GitHistoryReadError` whenever the repo is shallow.

**Not reachable in production at this sha** — `container.build_git_history_reader()` (`container.py:216`) has zero call sites outside `tests/`, and no CLI module references `migrate_v5`/`run_migration`. Every current construction site passes neither `history_reader` nor `repo_root`, so the method short-circuits to `None` before any git walk.

**Why it still matters:** `container.py:216`'s docstring names the CLI composition root as the intended next caller. On that day, a consumer whose workspace repo is a `git clone --depth 1` gets an uncaught `GitHistoryReadError` out of a read-only `bugs status`/`bugs stats` render instead of the documented `None` degrade — an availability regression on a display path.

Reproduce: `git clone --depth 1 file://<repo> /tmp/shallow`, then construct `BugService(..., history_reader=container.build_git_history_reader(), repo_root=Path('/tmp/shallow'))` and call `.resolved_commit(record)` on a record whose `resolved_commit is None`.
findings.fix_recommendation: Design call for software-architect + software-engineer: decide once whether the shallow condition is fatal (keep the raise; amend the A8.3 docstring; the future CLI caller catches and warns) or degradable (catch `GitHistoryReadError` in `BugService.resolved_commit`, return `None`, keep loudness for the migration/contract-test callers). Do NOT resolve it with a flag or a second code path.

findings.message: OPEN — the shallow guard is fail-open: a non-zero `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` exit silently restores the exact silent-under-report behaviour the guard exists to prevent.
findings.detail_md:
`dadaia_workspace/infrastructure/git_subprocess.py:444-450`

```python
shallow = _run_bytes(["git", "rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository"], cwd=repo)
if shallow.returncode == 0 and shallow.stdout.strip() == b"true":
    raise GitHistoryReadError(...)
```

The `returncode == 0` conjunct means any git that does not understand the flag (added in git 2.15) — or any unexpected rev-parse failure — falls through to the walk and produces the partial, plausible-looking history the guard was written to refuse. The opposite posture from the sibling error path in the same method, which fails CLOSED on a non-zero exit (`git_subprocess.py:465-470`).

Blast radius is small today: runner images and the local toolchain (git 2.43.0) support the flag, and a non-repo path fails closed one call later at the `git log` guard. The exposure is a consumer on an old or minimal git image.
findings.fix_recommendation: Make the guard fail closed like its sibling — `if shallow.returncode != 0 or shallow.stdout.strip() == b"true"`, with the message distinguishing 'shallow' from 'cannot determine depth'. One line, no new caller branch.

findings.message: Secrets/privacy lane clean: 138 added lines against origin/main carry no credential, key header, e-mail, IP, operator home path or private hostname; the merge adds zero lines.
findings.detail_md:
The content range is unchanged from the previous review (`origin/main..e9b0a1f2`, 138 `^+` lines over 9 files) because the merge is content-free. All classes zero: credential assignments, private-key headers, `/home`-`/Users`-`C:\Users`, e-mail addresses, IPv4, URLs, and `shell=True`/`os.system`/`eval(`/`exec(`.

The one address-shaped string in the touched area is `test@example.invalid`, a reserved-TLD placeholder in the pre-existing `_init_repo` helper, set repo-locally via `git config` (never `--global`).

The merge itself cannot introduce anything: whole-tree identity with its first parent means zero new blobs in the tree. The push-gate denylist scan did still run over the widened object range at this head (the merge pulls develop's objects into the pushed range) and reported no denylist hit — its exit 1 is the canon/verdict rule, a different check, quoted in the HIGH finding above.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action. Redaction discipline (DADAIA.md §9 / §7.3) holds across the whole range.

findings.message: Injection lane clean on both new subprocess call sites: static argv lists, no shell, no interpolated caller input.
findings.detail_md:
Carried by tree identity (`dadaia_workspace` and `tests` objects unchanged).

**1. `dadaia_workspace/infrastructure/git_subprocess.py:444`** — `_run_bytes(["git", "rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository"], cwd=repo)`: every argv element literal; `_run_bytes` is `subprocess.run(args, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True)`; `grep -n 'shell='` over the module returns nothing. `repo` is passed only as `cwd`; `pathspec` reaches only the exception message via `!r`, never argv, and the pre-existing `git log` call still places it after `--`. The byte comparison `shallow.stdout.strip() == b"true"` is CRLF-safe for the windows-latest runners.

**2. `tests/helpers/suite_files.py:19-24`** — `subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files", "-z", "--", "tests"], cwd=repo_root, capture_output=True, check=True)`: literal argv, `--` terminator, no shell. The `pattern` parameter never reaches git; it is applied in-process with `fnmatch.fnmatch` over the basename, so no glob or shell metacharacter is interpreted externally. `-z` correctly disables `core.quotePath` escaping, making the strict UTF-8 decode sound.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action.

findings.message: OPEN — double serialisation baked 13 literal `\u2014` escape sequences into log[24]'s narrative; the archived qa-close text reads `not most \u2014 rc-1` instead of an em dash.
findings.detail_md:
`specs/releases/_archive/0.5.0/RELEASE.json`, `log[24]` (`kind: "note"`). The normalisation moved the old `data` object into `text` by `json.dumps`-ing it; because an earlier commit had re-serialised the file with `ensure_ascii=True`, the source strings already carried `\u2014` escapes, and serialising a second time escaped the backslash.

| entry | `len(text)` | literal `\u` sequences | real em dashes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `log[24]` | 7 374 | **13** | **0** |
| `log[25]`/`[26]`/`[27]` | 366/276/221 | 0 | 0 |

No data lost and the document is schema-valid; the damage is legibility of an archived record the audit lane reads as evidence. It is a one-way ratchet: each further re-serialisation doubles the escaping again.
findings.fix_recommendation: product-engineer decodes `log[24]`'s text once and rewrites the entry with `ensure_ascii=False`, before the next write to this file since the escaping compounds.

findings.message: OPEN — machine-readable provenance (rc, sha, pr, merge, phase) was folded into free-text note bodies, so fields that used to be parseable now require prose parsing.
findings.detail_md:
At this head, `log[25]` (`kind: "rc"`) ends `… cleared by those fixes. {"rc": 1, "sha": "48d032dca6d6b4ceab3f0aea6e25cc68644bad8d", "pr": 219, "merge": "be4b2cc2"}`; `log[26]` and `log[27]` end similarly with `{"phase": …}` and `{"sha": …, "pr": 221}`.

Schema-COMPLIANT — `release-state-v1` calls `log` "the one place free-form governance narrative survives" and gives it no structured sub-fields — and **no value was lost**, which is why this is LOW. The typed milestones (`defined`/`implemented`/`shipped`/`audited`) remain the queryable home for the sha-bearing facts, so nothing an automated consumer needs is trapped in prose.
findings.fix_recommendation: No change requested. Read `log[25]`'s rc sha from the `implemented` milestone rather than parsing the note. Audit-lane note only.

findings.message: OPEN — two write-once governance fields were corrected in place, out-of-band of the `bugs update` seam that refuses such a re-set by design, after the branch had already been pushed to origin.
findings.detail_md:
`bug-record-v1.schema.json` marks both changed fields `"x-mutability": "write-once"` (`evidence_diff`, `diff_direction`). The CLI enforces that; a text edit to the JSONL does not, because `specs/bugs/**` is an ADDITIVE path whose record contract DADAIA.md §3.2 states is **"audited, not gated"**. This correction is exactly the class of event the audit lane exists to catch.

One factual correction to the justification: the pre-correction values did NOT stay local to the branch — the branch was published at earlier heads, so the wrong `diff_direction` was pushed. It was never merged to `develop`/`main` and no consumer read it, so practical impact is nil and I do not contest the fix; a truthful record is worth more than an untouched-but-wrong one.

Recorded because the alternative reading is the dangerous one: that a write-once field is editable whenever the CLI is inconvenient. It is not.
findings.fix_recommendation: project-auditor records this as a dispositioned carve-out in the next audit window, naming the two record ids and this sha. If in-branch correction of a not-yet-merged record is meant to be legitimate, product-engineer should give `bugs update` an explicit, evidence-bearing amend path so the next correction goes through the seam rather than around it.

findings.message: OPEN — ratchet scope narrows from the working tree to the git index: an unstaged new test file is outside all four ratchets, and the ratchets stop working outside a git checkout.
findings.detail_md:
`tests/helpers/suite_files.py::tracked_test_files` defines the suite as `git ls-files -- tests`, used by four walks (`test_test_suite_ratchets.py:136`, `:199`, `:264`, `test_frozen_clock_aging_ratchet.py:113`).

1. **Untracked == invisible.** A newly authored test file never `git add`ed is outside every ratchet, including the stewardship gates (intent-header coverage, SCAFFOLD expiry) that exist to catch undeclared tests at birth (DADAIA.md §7.2). A local preflight can go green on a file CI later ratchets. CI is unaffected — it runs on a committed tree — and `git ls-files` reads the INDEX, so a staged file still counts; the window is authored-but-never-staged only.
2. **git becomes a test dependency.** `check=True` makes the four ratchets raise `CalledProcessError` rather than skip outside a git checkout. Low impact: poetry packages only `dadaia_workspace`, so `tests/` never ships in the wheel.

A deliberate, defensible trade — it is what makes scratch probes out-of-scope by construction — recorded because the commit message does not call the narrowing out.
findings.fix_recommendation: No change requested. If the unstaged window matters, add a pre-commit warning; do not reintroduce per-ratchet exclusion branches, which is the shape this fix correctly deleted.

findings.message: No generated-file leakage from the test suite: the new test's scratch probe is written into an already-gitignored directory and cannot be committed.
findings.detail_md:
`test_ratchet_scope_is_the_tracked_suite_never_a_tests_tmp_probe` writes `tests/tmp/_ratchet_scope_probe.py` and removes it in a `finally`.

- `.gitignore:73-74` is `tests/tmp/*` + `!tests/tmp/README.md`; `git check-ignore -v` confirms the match. A probe left by a SIGKILLed run is untracked AND ignored, so it cannot be captured even by `git add -A`, and `git ls-files` — the helper's own definition of scope — excludes it by construction.
- `tests/tmp/` exists in-tree (only `README.md`), so `write_text` cannot fail on a missing parent.
- The probe name is distinct from the older sibling's and from the pid-suffixed stewardship probe, so no fixed-path collision between xdist workers is introduced.

Confirmed empirically: `pytest -n 2` on both ratchet files -> 11 passed, exit 0, `git status` clean of test residue. (The one uncommitted worktree entry at review time is `specs/backlog/BACKLOG.json`, unrelated to this PR and outside the reviewed tree.)
findings.fix_recommendation: No action.

findings.message: OPEN — duplicated invariant plus a slightly more brittle teardown: two tests assert the same tests/tmp exclusion through the same helper, and the new one drops `missing_ok=True`.
findings.detail_md:
`test_frozen_clock_aging_ratchet.py:199` and the new `test_test_suite_ratchets.py:505` now assert the same invariant, both reaching `tracked_test_files` (the older one through the `_test_files` shim this change reduced to a delegation). After the refactor the invariant has ONE implementation, so one test is redundant coverage of the other.

Teardown asymmetry: the older test uses `probe.unlink(missing_ok=True)`; the new one uses bare `probe.unlink()`, so if anything else removes the probe first the `finally` raises and masks the real assertion outcome.
findings.fix_recommendation: qa-engineer disposition under test stewardship (DADAIA.md §7.2): keep the invariant at the helper and retire the duplicate; add `missing_ok=True` in the same pass. Pruning is a qa-engineer verdict and execution is software-engineer's — never mine.

findings.message: OPEN — gitleaks never runs on a `feature/* -> develop` PR, so this PR gets no automated secret scan in CI.
findings.detail_md:
`.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml` triggers on `push: branches: [main, 'hotfix/v*']` and `pull_request: branches: [main]` only. This PR targets `develop`, so the gitleaks job is not in its check set. Pre-existing gap applying to EVERY feature->develop PR — the edge where new code first becomes reviewable.

Compensating controls exercised at this head: the added-line secret/privacy scan (0 matches over 138 lines) and the push-gate denylist scan (no denylist hit). Both are session-local; neither is enforced by CI on this edge. This also means the 40-hex allowlist finding above stays untested until the deploy PR.
findings.fix_recommendation: software-engineer adds `develop` to `secret-scan.yml`'s `pull_request.branches` so gitleaks gates the first publication edge, not only the deploy edge. Route via project-manager.

findings.message: Workflow lane: no permission, secret, token or action-pin change; `fetch-depth: 0` cannot reach a published artifact.
findings.detail_md:
`.github` is byte-identical to the previously reviewed tree (`ff5d53662a0206857f72b82e245369b1648a2cf6`), so this carries over by identity. The whole workflow diff against `origin/main` is six `with: fetch-depth: 0` blocks on `release.yml`'s `unit-fast`, `contract-coverage`, `integration`, `e2e-python`, `e2e-panel` and `build` checkouts.

- **Permissions unchanged.** Top-level `permissions: contents: read` (lines 7-8); only `publish` elevates (`contents: write`, `id-token: write`, lines 221-223). Neither block touched.
- **No secret introduced or widened.** No `secrets.*` reference and no `env:` entry added. OIDC trusted publishing remains the only credential path; `approve` still blocks on the `release-gate` environment.
- **Supply chain unchanged.** Every `uses:` stays pinned to a full commit sha with a version comment (OWASP A08); no action re-pointed, added or bumped.
- **Full history on the runner** is the only new exposure, already the repo's deliberate posture: all 15 `ci.yml` checkouts and `secret-scan.yml`'s checkout already use it. Runners are ephemeral, the repo is private, and `persist-credentials` behaves identically at depth 1 and depth 0.
- **The `build` job's full history cannot leak into the wheel/sdist**: `pyproject.toml:7` is `packages = [{include = "dadaia_workspace"}]`; `.git/` is outside it.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action.

findings.message: Two release.yml checkouts are intentionally left shallow; neither runs a history-dependent test, and a future miss is now self-announcing.
findings.detail_md:
8 `actions/checkout` steps in `release.yml`, 6 at `fetch-depth: 0`. The two at default depth-1: `check` (lines 19-21, `fetch-tags: true`) runs only a `grep` over `pyproject.toml` plus `git ls-remote --tags`; `publish` (line 226) does `git tag` + `git push origin <tag>` on HEAD, correct on a shallow clone. Both avoid a needless full clone on the credential-bearing job.

Residual risk is covered by the adapter guard: one loud `GitHistoryReadError` instead of 20 plausible-but-wrong derivations. Cross-check: `ci.yml` 15/15 full-history; `secret-scan.yml` 1/1. No workflow runs a history-dependent test on a shallow tree.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action.

findings.message: Dependency lane N/A: zero manifest or lockfile changes, zero new third-party imports, and the merge adds no content.
findings.detail_md:
The 9 changed paths against `origin/main` include no `pyproject.toml`, `poetry.lock`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json` or requirements file. New imports across the range are stdlib (`subprocess`, `fnmatch`, `pathlib`), `pytest`, and first-party modules. No dependency enters the graph and no installed version changes, so no CVE surface delta is attributable to this PR; the merge is content-free and cannot change this.

Per this reviewer's scope rule the PR-gate scan target is exactly the diff under review; a repo-wide `pip-audit`/`npm audit` sweep belongs to the audit lane and none was run.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action for this PR. Schedule the repo-wide CVE sweep with the next `project-auditor` window.

findings.message: Bug-surface axis: REDUCED on three counts — two duplicated-precondition classes collapsed to one definition each, plus a governance-record defect class driven to zero.
findings.detail_md:
**Axis 1 — shallow history.** Prior fix `contract-coverage-ci-shallow-checkout-collapses-resolved-commit-derivation-to-head` recorded `solution: "every ci.yml checkout runs with fetch-depth 0"` (+28 lines over 14 checkouts) — a per-call-site patch that left the class alive. Recurrence: `release-workflow-shallow-checkout-collapses-resolved-commit-derivation-to-head`, `caused_by` that record, same symptom from a different yaml file (Release run 33202885086 on main, 20 FAILED, every derived `resolved_commit == HEAD`). This fix states the precondition ONCE inside `GitSubprocessClient.log_added_lines` (+6 production lines, zero new caller-visible branches), covering both production callers by construction.

**Axis 2 — ratchet scope.** Prior fix `frozen-clock-ratchet-scans-tests-tmp-scratch-dir` excluded `tests/tmp` inside ONE walker. Recurrence: `v26-ratchet-scans-tests-tmp-scratch-dir-xdist-race`, CI run 33203537800, `FileNotFoundError` on a concurrent probe, because three other walks kept their own raw `rglob`/`glob`. Its `root_cause` names it exactly: *"Each ratchet re-implemented suite discovery, so the exclusion had to be repeated per walker — it was not."* This fix replaces 4 private walks with 1 shared enumeration and DELETES the special-case branch.

**Axis 3 — governance records.** RELEASE.json 12 schema errors -> 0 (including 3 pre-existing), BUGS.jsonl 10 invalid -> 8 (exactly this PR's two fixed).

| axis | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| shallow precondition, places stated | every checkout in every workflow | 1 (the adapter) |
| ratchet suite discovery, implementations | 4 walks + 1 exclusion branch | 1 helper, branch deleted |
| RELEASE.json schema errors | 12 | 0 |
| BUGS.jsonl invalid records | 10 | 8 (all pre-existing) |
| new caller-visible branches/flags | — | 0, every commit |

No fix adds a flag, special case, second code path, cross-feature reach-in or shared mutable state; each lands inside the unit that owns the contract it defends. **Bug surface REDUCED on every axis.**

Honest counterweights, so the claim is checkable: production/test line count GREW (+46 and net +39) — the reduction is in duplicated call sites and branches, not bytes, and the ledger now says so in its own `evidence_diff` instead of claiming a shrink. The residual MEDIUM (a raise on a documented never-raising resolver) is a small NEW surface this PR opens. And the merge commit, while content-free, ADDED one operational failure mode by staleness alone — the HIGH finding above — which is a real, if transient, surface increase in the release-governance lane.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action. Prefer this shape — precondition inside the owning unit's own contract, duplicated discovery collapsed to one definition — for the next recurrence of a per-call-site patch.

findings.message: Test hygiene clean: hermetic tmp_path repository, repo-local git config, self-created clone source, no network.
findings.detail_md:
`test_log_added_lines_refuses_a_shallow_repository`:

- The clone source is a repository the test creates under `tmp_path` in the same function, reached via `origin.as_uri()` (`file://`). No untrusted repository is ever cloned, so the local-clone code-execution class (CVE-2024-32004 and neighbours, which require a maliciously crafted source repo) does not apply.
- No network egress; marked `pytest.mark.slow`; runs under `tmp_path`, never inside the source tree.
- Identity set with repo-local `git config` (no `--global`); the only address-shaped string is the reserved-TLD `test@example.invalid`.
- `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)` throughout: no git output reaches the test log.
- Asserts on the exception class and the substring `"shallow"`, not on the absolute path the message interpolates, so the message can be redacted later without breaking the test.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action.

findings.message: OPEN — the new `GitHistoryReadError` message interpolates the absolute repository path, which can carry an operator-local path into a report, log or ledger field.
findings.detail_md:
`dadaia_workspace/infrastructure/git_subprocess.py:446-450`:

```python
f"{repo} is a shallow repository: a history walk over {pathspec!r} would ..."
```

`repo` is an absolute `Path`, so on a developer machine the message renders an operator home path. DADAIA.md §7.3 requires local paths, hostnames and private names to be redacted from every bug-ledger field, and an unhandled traceback is a common route into a pasted repro, a CI log or a `symptom` field.

LOW deliberately: the pattern is pre-existing and consistent — the sibling error twenty lines below does the same — so this adds an instance, not a class. The repo is private and no credential is interpolated.

findings.message: OPEN — `shipped.sha` remains the 8-hex abbreviation `9ebefd5f` while every sibling milestone carries a full 40-hex value.
findings.detail_md:
`specs/releases/_archive/0.5.0/RELEASE.json` -> `shipped.sha = "9ebefd5f"`, and the same abbreviated value in `releases_histo.jsonl`'s shipped record, versus `audited.sha = "5c0448dcc1feeec204e24b4b4583618017f6c52b"` in the same document. Still present at this head — the normalisation touched only the `log` array.

`release-state-v1.schema.json` places no length constraint on milestone `sha`, so this is schema-legal — but an abbreviated sha is an ambiguity-prone evidence anchor, and every sha-consuming gate here is written for 40-hex (`pr-verdict-check.sh` shape-checks `PR_HEAD_SHA` as 40-hex before it reaches any git argv). Provenance a gate cannot ingest verbatim is weak provenance.
findings.fix_recommendation: product-engineer back-fills the full 40-hex value in both files; tighten the schema's milestone `sha` to `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` so the next writer cannot abbreviate.

findings.message: Commit-message accuracy note carried forward: an earlier commit's subject claims a `specs/AGENTS.md` refresh that the tree does not contain.
findings.detail_md:
`e9b0a1f2`'s subject ends *"specs/AGENTS.md refreshed to canonical template"*, but `git diff --name-only d9f9685c..e9b0a1f2` returns only `specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl` and `specs/releases/_archive/0.5.0/RELEASE.json`. The `specs doctor --fix` invocation evidently found no difference and correctly wrote nothing, but the subject asserts a change the tree does not carry.

Zero security impact; recorded because commit subjects are the audit lane's cheapest index into what a commit did, and a subject that overstates its own diff degrades that index — the same evidence-integrity concern as the record findings, one layer out.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action on the pushed commit. Prefer subjects that describe the realised diff; where a `--fix` invocation is a no-op, say so or omit the clause.

decisions_required: DO THIS FIRST, in ONE commit on feature/0.5.1: delete specs/releases/0.5.1/verdicts/e9b0a1f2035b35ea1558e2bb79b9f32593895be3.handoff.json and add this handoff as specs/releases/0.5.1/verdicts/3b69f1d28d37ddaaa6d9e1e5aaf4b36740cf6ba7.handoff.json. Verify with `dadaia specs doctor` and `dadaia ci push-gate-check` BEFORE pushing.

Do NOT run `dadaia specs doctor --fix` on its own to clear the error: it deletes the stale verdict and leaves the branch with no committed evidence at all, which turns a push-gate failure into a CI verdict-gate failure. Do NOT push with --no-verify — this has a clean one-commit fix.

Note on gate arithmetic, so nobody is surprised: after that commit the head moves again, but the new verdict's commit_sha will then be the first parent and the only differing path will be verdict-anchored — satisfying SPEC-DOC-044 and pr-verdict-check.sh simultaneously. Committing the verdict alone is what makes that true; bundling any other change into the commit breaks the coverage proof.

Owner of the one remaining MEDIUM: the resolver-contract tension (raise vs degrade on a shallow repo) is a software-architect/software-engineer design call, decided once, with no new flag. It does not block this merge because no production call site wires the history reader today.
